newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen falling as economy hopes fizzle.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen falling as economy hopes fizzle.

text.p: Seoul stocks are forecast to decline on Friday with blue chips pressured because of fizzling hopes about the economy's recovery, brokers said.
They said the economic optimism, sparked most recently by an improvement in the June trade balance, was losing ground in the absence of additional good news.
The troubled Jinro Group's affiliates are expected to remain firmer on the group's plan to generate some 840 billion won by selling most of its affiliates and some real estate.
The composite index fell 4.22 points to 767.77 on Thursday.
Three listed Jinro Group affiliates went limit-up on Thursday after the group announced the sales plan. The group was selected for bailout in April by its creditor banks.
"Investors are becoming increasingly doubtful that the economy has passed the hard times," said Chang Kun-woo of Daishin Securities.
Relatively tight liquidity on the money market is also discouraging investors, brokers said.
"It's unusual that liquidity has continued to be tight during the early part of a month," said Kim Chun-kon of Daewoo Securities. --YOO CHOON-SIK (822) 727 5646
